details: It rained until the third hour.
The wind carried ash from the west.
Somewhere a dog barked and was stopped.
A bell rang once and was not answered.
The fog came up to the knee.
Frost on the cobbles by dawn.
Smoke from the tanneries hung low.
A cart went by with no driver.
The candles burned green for a moment.
Somebody was singing in the Poor Quarter. Badly.
A crow followed for three streets.
The stars were out. All of them.
Wet plaster. Old blood. Bread, from somewhere.
The Watch did not pass all night.
closers: Nobody spoke of the road south.
The door stayed barred until first light.
The fire was let go out.
Somebody had left bread on the step.
The night was not mentioned again.
The ledger was written by candle.

boon: {name} went sifting in {district}. {they} came back with green in both pockets and no words about how.
{first} turned over half a cellar in {district}. Under the last stone, a glow.
{name} found where the ash was warm in {district} and dug until it was not. Two slivers, and a hand that shakes a little.
{first} came back from {district} before dawn, walking carefully. The pockets were the reason.
fair: {name} sifted the rubble in {district} until the light went. One sliver, small, and a bad feeling about the far wall.
{first} worked {district} alone. A sliver of green, a broken buckle, and a street that is not on the map.
{name} spent the night in {district} moving stones. One of them was worth moving.
{first} came back from {district} with a sliver and a story about a door that was not there the night before.
poor: {name} sifted {district} until the third hour and found only bones. Not fresh ones. Not old enough.
{first} went into {district} and came back with dust, a cough, and nothing green.
{name} turned {district} over stone by stone. Somebody had been there first, and recently.
{first} lost the night to a collapsed stair in {district}. Nothing was found. Nothing was lost but the night.
standing: {name} kept to the usual rubble in {district}. The usual haul.
{first} sifted {district} out of habit and came back out of habit.

boon: {name} drank in {district} with men who talk. By midnight the whole tavern knew {their} name and half of them owed {them}.
{first} held the table at {district} until the candles went. Nobody remembers who paid. Everybody remembers {first}.
{name} sang in {district}. It should not have worked. It worked.
{first} lost the first three games in {district} and won the rest. The city likes a comeback.
fair: {name} drank in {district} and listened more than {they} spoke. The right people noticed.
{first} bought a round in {district} and was bought two back. A fair night. A fair head, tomorrow.
{name} sat with the boatmen in {district}. They know {their} face now.
{first} found the back room at {district}. Nothing was decided. Nothing was lost.
poor: {name} drank in {district} and said too much to the wrong table. It will keep.
{first} came back from {district} without {their} purse and with a song nobody asked for.
{name} was asked to leave {district}. Politely, the first time.
{first} drank alone in {district}. The tavern was quiet. So was the city's regard.
standing: {name} kept the usual stool in {district}. The usual company.
{first} drank in {district} and was neither remembered nor forgotten.

boon: {name} took a bout at the Pit under {omen}. The crowd wanted blood. {first} gave them a name instead.
{first} fought three rounds in {district} against a man twice {their} weight. The man is still explaining it.
{name} drilled in {district} until the moves stopped being moves. Someone was watching. Someone always is.
{first} won at the Pit without drawing steel. The wagers paid out. The story paid better.
fair: {name} sparred in {district} until {their} arms were lead. Nothing learned that will not hurt tomorrow.
{first} took a bout at the Pit and took a bruise for it. The crowd was fair. The crowd is never fair.
{name} practised the same cut two hundred times in {district}. The last twenty were right.
{first} watched the Pit more than {they} fought it. That is also training.
poor: {name} fought at the Pit and lost in the first minute. The crowd had barely sat down.
{first} drilled in {district} and pulled something. The something has opinions.
{name} was paired against a Sister at the Pit. It did not last. {first} does not want to discuss it.
{first} went to the Pit, found it closed, and stood in the rain for a while out of principle.
standing: {name} drilled in {district} as {they} always do. The blade is no duller.
{first} kept the forms in {district}. Nobody watched.

boon: {name} lay in a gutter in {district} for four hours and heard everything that mattered and two things that did not.
{first} followed a lantern through {district} to a door, and stayed until the door said something.
{name} paid a child in {district} a penny for a rumour and got three. Two were true.
{first} sat under the window in {district} where the wrong people meet. They met.
fair: {name} listened at the well in {district}. Half a name and a direction.
{first} watched the {rival} camp from a roof in {district}. Somebody there was awake too.
{name} traded a rumour for a rumour in {district}. Fair exchange. Cold by next Moon.
{first} learned which alley in {district} the Watch does not walk. It may be useful. It may be why.
poor: {name} was seen in {district}. Not caught. Seen.
{first} listened at a door in {district} for two hours. It was the wrong door.
{name} followed a man through {district} who turned out to be following {them}.
{first} spent the night in {district} learning that nobody talks under {omen}.
standing: {name} kept an ear open in {district}. Nothing worth the ink.
{first} watched the usual corner in {district}. The usual nothing.

boon: {name} kept the candles at {district} until dawn. Every one of them held. The Sisters noticed, which is rarer than a blessing.
{first} knelt in {district} until the stone hurt. Something answered. {first} will not say what.
{name} lit a candle in {district} for each of the dead. There was wax to spare. There is never wax to spare.
{first} prayed in {district} with the door open. Nothing came in. That was the answer.
fair: {name} kept the candles at {district}. They held until the third hour.
{first} sat with Sister Agathe in {district} and said little. The saying was not the point.
{name} prayed in {district} and felt, for a moment, watched over. Or watched.
{first} lit one candle in {district} and it did not go out. Take that as given.
poor: {name} kept the candles at {district}. The draught got them one by one.
{first} prayed in {district} and heard only the rain. It is possible the rain was the answer.
{name} went to {district} and found the shrine already full. Stood at the back. Left early.
{first} knelt in {district} until the doubt was louder than the prayer.
standing: {name} lit the usual candle in {district}. It burned as usual.
{first} said the words in {district}. They were the right words.

boon: {name} met Henrik in {district} and let the silence do the haggling. Henrik broke first.
{first} moved the green in {district} to a man who did not ask where it came from and paid as if he knew.
{name} sold a story in {district} along with the goods. The story fetched more.
{first} found a fence in {district} who owed the {rival} money. Interesting rates.
fair: {name} traded in {district}. Fair weight, fair price, a chit for later.
{first} spent the night in {district} arguing over a sliver. The argument was the entertainment.
{name} came back from {district} with less green and more coin. About the same weight.
{first} watched Henrik weigh everything twice in {district}. The second time was the price.
poor: {name} went to {district} to trade and found the fence gone and his shutters open. Nothing was taken but the night.
{first} was offered a price in {district} that was an insult and took the long way home thinking about it.
{name} traded in {district} and got a chit that turned out to be a receipt for something else.
{first} waited in {district} for a buyer who sent word at midnight that he was dead. Possibly true.
standing: {name} kept the usual arrangement in {district}. The usual coin.
{first} traded in {district} the way {they} always do. Henrik nodded.

pairs: {other} waited at the corner with a lantern and did not need to use it.
{other} came back first and did not say why.
The two of them did not speak on the way home.
{other} kept watch on the door. Nobody tried it.
rumours: The Sisters are buying candles by the crate.
Somebody is paying for names of the dead.
The fence on the Rock has a new scale and an old debt.
There is a bell under the ash in the Poor Quarter. It rings at the third hour.
The Watch has stopped walking the tannery lane. Nobody asked them to.
A ship with no name is anchored below the bridge.
The {rival} lost something in the cellars. They want it back.
The Pit has a new champion. Nobody has seen his face.
Old Henrik weighs shards twice now. The first weight is for you.
A child in the Merchant's Quarter sells true rumours for a penny. Only one per customer.
The Man in Grey was seen at the Ostermark Gate. He was not going in.
Someone has been carving names on the Broken Bell. Not the dead ones.
return: The door had swollen in the frame. Somebody had left bread.
The candles had burned to the sockets. Someone had replaced them.
The city had not noticed. The city never does. The rain had kept the step clean.
cityProvides: A bone charm on the step, wrapped in a rag. No note.
A child at the corner hands over a folded paper and runs.
Under the door at dusk: a fence's chit, unsigned.
quiet: The door stayed barred. Nobody went out. The city went on without them.
A night in. The fire held. The count was taken.
